signature.name: Pyramids of Giza
signature.detail: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world and the reason many people come to Egypt. Go early in the morning to beat the heat and crowds, and wear comfortable shoes for the sand and stone.

signature.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
signature.detail: The iconic limestone statue with a human head and lion body, guarding the Giza plateau. It is included with the Giza site ticket; visit at opening time for the best light and fewer people.

signature.name: Egyptian Museum
signature.detail: Home to a vast collection of ancient Egyptian artifacts, including royal mummies and treasures. Allow at least two hours; tickets are sold at the entrance and photography may require an extra fee.

signature.name: Cairo Citadel
signature.detail: A medieval Islamic fortification offering panoramic views over Cairo. Wear modest clothing as it contains active mosques, and go in the late afternoon for cooler weather.

signature.name: Mosque of Muhammad Ali
signature.detail: The striking alabaster mosque inside the Citadel, a symbol of Ottoman Cairo. Remove your shoes before entering and dress conservatively; it is busiest around midday prayer.

signature.name: Khan el-Khalili
signature.detail: A historic bazaar full of shops, cafés and narrow alleys, perfect for souvenirs and people-watching. Visit in the evening when it is liveliest, and be ready to bargain.

food: Casual meal $5-10; street food like kushari under $3
transport: Metro ride under $0.50; taxis and ride-hailing cheap
